name: Quadratic assignment, QAPLIB sko64
description: Quadratic assignment problem, QAPLIB instance sko64: given two 64 x 64 integer matrices a and b, find a permutation p of 0..63 that minimises the cost, the sum over all i and j of a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]]. In the usual reading one matrix holds the flows between facilities and the other the distances between locations, and p assigns the one to the other; the cost formula is what is scored.

execution.interface: solve(a, b) -> permutation p of 0..n-1 (a list of n integers, each exactly once). a and b are the first and second matrix of the QAPLIB file (int64 arrays of shape (n, n), passed as copies). Score: the exact integer cost, the sum over all i and j of a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]], minimized.

science_relevance.reason: Each cited paper has the quadratic assignment problem, or the search for good QAPLIB solutions, as its main objective; the evaluator scores exactly the QAP cost of a permutation on the pinned instance.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a minimum-cost Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment of 64 facilities to 64 locations for the QAPLIB instance sko64, which is not solved to optimality.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The quadratic assignment problem models facility and hospital layout, keyboard design, backboard wiring and the generation of grey patterns. It is NP-hard and hard in practice: QAPLIB instances above about 30 facilities are mostly unsolved, and the best known solutions of the larger ones have stood for many years, so a cheaper permutation is a new best known solution of a standard open instance.

papers.title: Assignment Problems and the Location of Economic Activities
papers.task_relation: The task's objective is the Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment cost of the QAPLIB instance sko64.
papers.primary_goal: Formulate the assignment of indivisible economic activities to locations, introducing the quadratic assignment problem.

papers.title: Tabu Search Applied to the Quadratic Assignment Problem
papers.task_relation: QAPLIB credits the Skorin-Kapov instance set (rectangular-grid distances, pseudorandom flows) to this paper, and lists strict tabu search from it as a heuristic; sko64 belongs to that set.
papers.primary_goal: Apply tabu search to the quadratic assignment problem.

papers.title: Robust taboo search for the quadratic assignment problem
papers.task_relation: QAPLIB credits the best known solution of sko64 to robust tabu search (Ro-TS), which this paper introduces; the task asks to improve it.
papers.primary_goal: Introduce the robust tabu search heuristic for the quadratic assignment problem and report results on test instances.
